note: No animal has PNH and most members bind only human C5, so the class relied on an in-vitro complement hemolysis assay in human serum, human-C5 mice or cynomolgus monkeys for duration, and human C5-deficiency genetics for infection risk.

dose.model: Human-C5-supplemented NOD-scid mice (ravulizumab vs eculizumab PK/PD)
dose.note: Mice given human C5 showed >3-fold longer ravulizumab half-life than eculizumab; patients' 8-weekly regimen kept free C5 suppressed for 26 weeks.
dose.quote: complete inhibition of serum free C5 levels < 0.5 µg/mL (correlated with inhibition of intravascular hemolysis and LDH lowering) was observed by the end of the first dose and sustained throughout the entire 26‐week treatment period
dose.confidence_note: Bundle text of the FDA review; contiguous excerpt of a longer sentence.
dose.judgement: The mouse predicted duration relative to eculizumab, not an absolute human regimen, so magnitude is direction_only. Model side, same review: 'ravulizumab showed no antigen‐mediated clearance through Day 28 and a greater than 3‐fold longer half‐life than eculizumab in the presence of C5'. Human terminal half-life 49.7 days (same review); against eculizumab's ~11 days from memory of the Soliris label (not re-checked here) the human ratio is ~4x, close to the mouse. The 175 µg/mL trough target came from patient PK/PD, not from the mouse. Opener is the monkey (first public dose model of the class); this entry is a different model, hence model_change true.
dose.magnitude_basis: duration of C5 blockade relative to eculizumab

dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey PK/PD (crovalimab cross-reacts with monkey C5)
dose.note: COMPOSER: crovalimab troughs stayed above the prespecified 100 µg/mL on weekly subcutaneous dosing, with complete terminal complement blockade.
dose.quote: Crovalimab concentrations exceeded the prespecified 100-µg/mL level and resulted in complete and sustained terminal complement pathway inhibition in treatment-naive and C5 inhibitor–pretreated PNH patients.
dose.confidence_note: PMC full text read by targeted extraction, not end to end.
dose.judgement: Scored same on the regimen the monkey supported (infrequent subcutaneous dosing after one IV load); the phase 3 regimen became every 4 weeks (FDA crovalimab review 2024), longer than the biweekly interval Fukuzawa proposed. One part did not hold: Fukuzawa argued a recycling antibody needs 'a much lower trough concentration' than the ~99 µg/mL a conventional antibody needs, yet patients needed ~100 µg/mL (FDA: 'concentrations above approximately 100 μg/mL resulted in complete inhibition'). I scored the regimen, not the trough claim, and record it here; a stricter reader could call the trough off_by_>5x unquantified. Registry NCT03157635 has no posted results.
dose.magnitude_basis: subcutaneous dosing interval sustaining complete blockade

efficacy.model: In-vitro complement hemolysis assay in human serum (no animal model of PNH)
efficacy.note: Ravulizumab met non-inferiority to eculizumab on transfusion avoidance and LDH normalization in complement-naive PNH (Study 301).
efficacy.quote: Non‐inferiority of ravulizumab compared to eculizumab was demonstrated across all efficacy endpoints in the complement inhibitor naïve treatment population using both sponsor’s and FDA recommended NIMs.
efficacy.confidence_note: Bundle text of the FDA review (FDA's own assessment, not the applicant's).
efficacy.judgement: Non-inferiority to an active comparator is scored as the predicted effect because the assay predicted complete C5 blockade, the same as eculizumab; there is no placebo trial for any member. Every other member's PNH trial agrees (patient_trials), so no member has a failure and neg is unavailable. Tesidolumab is the sharpest test of the assay: it predicted response in C5-variant patients whom eculizumab fails, and they responded. FDA noted ravulizumab missed non-inferiority on hemoglobin stabilization in Study 302, a key secondary, not the primary.

patient_trials.quote: Crovalimab completely blocked the terminal complement pathway activity (<10 U/mL) in all treatment-naive patients and patients who switched to crovalimab
In summary, tesidolumab had a favorable safety profile and was efficacious for PNH patients with either variant or non-variant C5.
Percentage of Participants Who Achieved Adequate Control of Intravascular Hemolysis (primary outcome; registry value 75.0%)

Overall, the persuasive results make reliance on a single, adequate, and well-controlled study, with confirmatory evidence from relevant pharmacodynamic/mechanistic data, appropriate to support approval in this rare, serious, and life-threatening disease.

safety.note: Neisserial risk reasoned from C5-deficient humans; the ravulizumab Phase 3 required meningococcal vaccination before dosing.

safety.model: Inherited human C5 deficiency (natural genetic model); mouse surrogate BB5.1 toxicology
safety.note: Three ravulizumab-treated PNH patients had meningococcal infection or sepsis, as C5-deficiency biology predicted; surrogate-antibody mouse toxicology was silent.
safety.quote: In the ULTOMIRIS clinical development program, a total of 3 patients with PNH (in the Phase 1b and 2 studies) experienced meningococcal infections/sepsis.
safety.confidence_note: Bundle text of the FDA review.
safety.judgement: Scored on the model the class relied on for infection risk, human terminal-complement-deficiency genetics, not the animal package: ravulizumab has no cross-reactive species, so toxicology used the murine anti-mouse-C5 surrogate BB5.1 (FDA review), which could not show Neisseria susceptibility and is not scored as a miss. The prediction also rests on eculizumab's patient experience (a non-member); I treat that as part of the model side, not as scored patient data. None of the infections occurred in the Phase 3 trials, which vaccinated everyone.

safety.short: Predicted immune complexes formed on switch
safety.quote: As expected, formation of drug-target-drug complexes was observed in all 19 patients switching to crovalimab, manifesting as transient mild or moderate vasculitic skin reactions in 2 of 19 participants.

safety.judgement: Different model from the previous entry, so model_change true. The paper states the prediction ('DTDCs are expected to develop if patients are exposed to crovalimab and eculizumab simultaneously (supplemental Figure 2)') and the result ('As predicted, DTDCs ... were detected in all switch patients'), so comparison_stated is true. The FDA 2024 review says the in-vitro analysis flagged hypersensitivity risk and that DTDC formation was not studied in animals. Cynomolgus arteritis tied to anti-drug antibodies was judged by FDA not predictive of humans and is not scored; monkey injection-site findings matched clinical injection reactions but are not scored separately.
